title: Scrub typhus
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Suspect in acute undifferentiated fever, especially with an eschar. Treat empirically without waiting for serology: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days (azithromycin in pregnancy). For severe disease give IV doxycycline plus IV azithromycin for 7 days (INTREST).

sections.title: Recognise
items: Suspected case (ICMR): acute undifferentiated fever of 5 days or more, with or without eschar; consider earlier if an eschar is present. Exposure to fields, bushes, scrub or rodents; peaks in monsoon and post-monsoon.

Eschar: painless, non-itchy black crust about 1 cm across, often with regional lymphadenopathy. Examine the axillae, groin, genitals, inframammary folds, waist and behind the ears; tender regional nodes point to a hidden eschar.
Other clues: headache, myalgia, conjunctival injection, maculopapular rash (a minority), hepatosplenomegaly, oedema.
Suggestive labs: normal or low white count early, thrombocytopenia, raised transaminases, hyponatraemia, hypoalbuminaemia, raised CRP.

Systemic presentations: pneumonitis or ARDS, meningoencephalitis or acute encephalitis syndrome, acute kidney injury, myocarditis, shock, hepatitis. Consider scrub typhus in every AES or community-acquired pneumonia in endemic areas.

sections.title: Investigations
items: IgM ELISA (preferred): positive if optical density above 0.5; usually positive after the first week of illness.
Weil-Felix OX-K titre of 1:80 or more suggests infection; poor sensitivity, so a negative result does not exclude it.
PCR on eschar material or whole blood confirms (best in the first week; yield falls after doxycycline). A fourfold rise in paired sera also confirms. Rapid card tests are not recommended by IAP.
Always test for malaria and dengue in parallel, and consider leptospirosis and enteric fever; co-infection occurs.
Severe disease: blood gas and lactate, renal and liver function, CPK, chest X-ray, ECG and troponin, CSF if encephalopathic.

sections.title: Uncomplicated disease
items: Start treatment on clinical suspicion; do not wait for serology.
Adults (45 kg or more): doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 7 days.

Children: doxycycline 2.2 mg/kg twice daily if under 40 kg (100 mg twice daily if 40 kg or more) for 7 days or until 3 days after defervescence (IAP). Short courses at any age do not cause tooth staining.
Alternative: azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 5 days (children 10 mg/kg/day for 5 days).

Expect defervescence within 48 hours of doxycycline. Persistent fever beyond 48 hours: reconsider the diagnosis, look for co-infection or complications, and consider adding or switching to azithromycin.
Do not use fluoroquinolones or beta-lactams for scrub typhus; sulfonamides are contraindicated and rifampicin is not for routine use.

sections.title: Severe disease (organ dysfunction)
items: Severe: any organ involvement, such as hypoxia or ARDS, shock, AKI, jaundice or hepatitis, encephalopathy, myocarditis. Admit; ICU if on vasopressors or ventilation.

Adults and adolescents (15 years or more): IV doxycycline 200 mg twice daily on day 1 then 100 mg twice daily, PLUS IV azithromycin 500 mg twice daily on day 1 then 500 mg once daily, for 7 days in total.

INTREST (NEJM 2023, 794 patients in India): the combination reduced the composite of death, persistent complications or persistent fever to 33%, versus 47% with doxycycline and 48% with azithromycin alone.

If IV doxycycline is unavailable, many centres give it orally or by nasogastric tube alongside IV azithromycin. IV chloramphenicol 50 to 100 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses (ICMR) is an older alternative with marrow toxicity.

Children with severe disease: IV doxycycline 2.2 mg/kg 12-hourly (maximum 100 mg per dose) or IV azithromycin 10 mg/kg/day; severe cases may need 10 days (IAP). Combination evidence is from patients aged 15 years and over.
Supportive care: lung-protective ventilation for ARDS, cautious fluids (capillary leak), noradrenaline for shock, renal replacement for AKI.

sections.title: Pregnancy and special groups
items: Pregnancy: azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 5 days (ICMR); doxycycline is avoided. Scrub typhus in pregnancy carries a risk of fetal loss; involve obstetrics.
G6PD deficiency, diabetes, younger age, absence of rash and delayed treatment are associated with worse outcomes (IAP).
Empirical doxycycline for undifferentiated fever with negative malaria and dengue tests is an accepted option in endemic areas (ICMR).

sections.title: Prevention
items: Protective clothing, insect repellent on skin and clothing, avoid sitting or lying on grass and bushes; bathe after field exposure.
No vaccine or post-exposure prophylaxis is available.
For short, high-risk exposures IAP suggests weekly doxycycline, started before and continued for 6 weeks after exposure.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Not examining the whole body for an eschar, especially the groin, axilla and under the breasts.
Waiting for IgM ELISA before treating; serology is often negative in the first week.
Relying on a negative Weil-Felix test.
Treating severe undifferentiated fever with ceftriaxone or piperacillin-tazobactam alone without doxycycline or azithromycin cover.
Aggressive fluid loading in a patient with capillary leak and pneumonitis.

drugs.name: Doxycycline (oral)
drugs.dose: Adults 100 mg twice daily for 7 days; children under 40 kg 2.2 mg/kg twice daily, 40 kg or more 100 mg twice daily
drugs.notes: Children: 7 days or 3 days after defervescence; severe cases may need 10 days. Avoid in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Doxycycline (IV), severe disease
drugs.dose: 200 mg IV twice daily on day 1, then 100 mg IV twice daily, total 7 days (with IV azithromycin)
drugs.notes: INTREST regimen for patients aged 15 years and over.

drugs.name: Azithromycin (oral)
drugs.dose: Adults 500 mg once daily for 5 days; children 10 mg/kg once daily for 5 days
drugs.notes: Drug of choice in pregnancy; alternative when doxycycline cannot be used.

drugs.name: Azithromycin (IV), severe disease
drugs.dose: 500 mg IV twice daily on day 1, then 500 mg IV once daily, total 7 days (with IV doxycycline)
drugs.notes: INTREST regimen. Check QTc with other QT-prolonging drugs.

drugs.name: Chloramphenicol (IV)
drugs.dose: 50 to 100 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (6-hourly)
drugs.notes: Alternative only when doxycycline and azithromycin cannot be used; monitor blood counts.
